source.title: Learning Capacity: A Measure of the Effective Dimensionality of a Model
source.authors: Dai-Wei Chen; Wei-Kai Chang; Pratik Chaudhari

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It varies fully connected network width and examines test loss against model size, addressing V2 with a different presentation of the width sweep. It also studies learning capacity as a generalization measure, which no listed version specifically names.
record.gate_note: The paper reports other results about learning capacity and test loss that do not measure a behavior named in V1 or V3–V8. It does not test random-label memorization, dropout, optimizer or batch-size comparisons as defined in the versions, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study reports width-dependent double descent for ResNet-18 on noisy CIFAR-10, bearing on V2 in a new setting, and directly compares convolutional and fully connected classifiers on binary MNIST, bearing on V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors propose learning capacity as an effective-dimensionality and model-selection measure, report useful test-loss correlations in many settings with a WikiText-2 exception, and find that plotting against learning capacity removes double descent. They do not show that double descent disappears when performance is plotted against network width.
record.recipe_differences: The paper estimates learning capacity using cross-validation and studies test loss against learning capacity and model size; it does not reproduce the specified post-interpolation width experiment with an extracted numerical result.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported learning-capacity and test-loss relationship varies by dataset: the authors report good correlation on MNIST and CIFAR-10, but poor correlation on WikiText-2.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning capacity correlates with test loss across image architectures, but the reported across-model correlation is poor on WikiText-2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning capacity can predict relative test loss across some architectures and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing parameter count with learning capacity removes the reported double-descent pattern; the test-loss slope is positive at smaller sample sizes and not significantly different from zero at N=50,000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test loss has a different relationship to estimated learning capacity than to network width or parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure S.4 reports similar test loss for width-factor-8 Wide-ResNet trained with SGD and width-factor-4 Wide-ResNet trained with Adam.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These two architecture-and-optimizer recipes obtain similar test loss; this comparison does not isolate an optimizer effect.

record.problems: The paper reports the width-versus-parameter-count result as a figure, without textual numerical values for the width sweep or its relation to the interpolation threshold. The authors also report poor learning-capacity/test-loss correlation on WikiText-2 and note uncertainty in some estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No rows are retained. Figure 4 depicts a fully connected width sweep on MNIST, but the text gives no assignable numerical values or explicit description of the post-interpolation portion for V2. Other findings concern learning capacity rather than a measure named by the versions.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.

Zero training error and the interpolation threshold are not reported. Training uses a fixed 200 epochs rather than demonstrated convergence. The MNIST width sweep reports test loss rather than classification error; the original downsampled CIFAR-10 setting is not reproduced.
The contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse connections, convolutional initialization of fully connected networks, and comparisons on CIFAR-100 and SVHN.
A controlled adaptive-optimizer comparison under specified tuning budgets. Figure S.4 changes both optimizer and network width.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations of the large-batch training recipe.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its relationship to generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and comparing retraining accuracy with random removal.

missing.what: The ResNet-18 width sweep reports double descent in test error on CIFAR-10 with noise rate 0.2 and N=50,000. Extract the qualitative result and recover numerical values only if the figure permits; do not infer the interpolation threshold from the caption.
missing.locator: Figure 4, lower-left panel and caption; Appendix D.

missing.what: The direct MNIST architecture comparison: LeNet test accuracy 98.9±0.1% and test loss 0.04±0.01 versus FC-1-100 accuracy 97.6±0.1% and loss 0.09±0.01, at N=50,000. The task is binary even-versus-odd classification.

record.verdict_notes: The empty record overlooks the numerical V3 comparison and the noisy-CIFAR-10 V2 experiment. The MNIST width sweep was explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so it is not listed as missing. Figure 4's caption mixes panel references and loss/error terminology; the lower-left plot is explicitly labeled Test Error. Neither a change of capacity coordinate nor learning-capacity/PAC-Bayes agreement tests V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural labels.
The paper shows a width sweep for fully connected networks on MNIST, but the figure-only evidence does not provide a textual result that can be assigned to post-interpolation test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons on images and the specified initialization or local-connection comparisons.
The specified adaptive-optimizer comparisons and tuning conditions.
The specified large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Dropout comparisons and the specified training-set and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness comparisons and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples and comparison with random removal.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 widths 1–64 on CIFAR-10 with 20% label noise and N=50,000.
relationships.reason: Based on text rather than extracted rows: Figure 4 explicitly reports double descent for the width sweep, whose plotted outcome is test error. This supports the descending wide-network regime, although zero training error is not documented.
relationships.display_finding: The reported decline in the wider-network regime remains unverified, and zero training error was undocumented.
